statement: afflom/verdant-studio is a video-game Lifecycle Management model, built only in Prism, using Verdant Engine as its only engine, applying its own lifecycle model to itself, and shipping as one application on its GitHub Pages.

The first rule that applies settles a question: a standard applies, so implement it; Prism or Verdant has a pattern, so reuse it unchanged; neither exists, so extrapolate a canonical schema, prove it locally and cite the nearest authority.
All work goes through the repository API. Machine-readable standards are generated. Inference only writes encodings where no machine-readable form exists.
A construct enters only with one citation: Std, Req or Der (D12).
Verdant Engine is the only engine, and Verdant Studio covers its whole public API.
Use an external oracle, or failing that an official machine-readable form; otherwise a locally proved encoding, reported separately.
Qortara adds no overhead; nothing is adopted.
The model comes first; a part is served only when it is relevant and verified.
Admitted ratchet checks are implemented in Prism inside Verdant Studio.
Development is mechanical and goes only through the API.
Every parameter and UI component is defined in Prism and traced to a stakeholder requirement.
Stakeholders are PROV-O producers and consumers; each requirement has one origin: identity, refinement or constraint.
The workspace has its own identity, separate from the owner, so the implementing agent runs the full lifecycle only through the repository API and the owner approves the pull requests it opens.
Models cross-classify each other, and relevance and differentiation are computed from that.

Verdant Studio is implemented in Verdant Studio: its entire production, every part of its model, is made in Verdant Studio, so that its UI is beautiful, refined, cohesive, illustrative and best-in-class for each part's domain use.
Verdant Studio is differentiated from its managed content, so that its features are never conflated with its demos, examples or pipelines.
